segments.content:
Chapter 258?

Riding the wave of popularity, Youke seized the opportunity to release the news: Legends of the Three Kingdoms' peak concurrent users exceeded 500,000!

The industry was shocked.

Truly shocked.

Because as popular as *Audition Online* was this year, its peak concurrent users only reached 400,000.

How could *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* possibly surpass *Audition Online*?

Alas, though the number of players was high, the revenue was not comparable.

Over 60% of *Audition Online*'s players were female, and those cool fashion items sold very well. Whether it was players competing with each other or opposite genders gifting each other items, hormones were stimulating consumption.

With 400,000 peak concurrent users, *Audition Online*'s monthly revenue could reach 50 million RMB, even more profitable than a pay-to-win game like *Reign of Hegemon*.

Of course, *Reign of Hegemon*'s revenue was still steadily increasing.

In comparison, *PopKart*, with 300,000 peak concurrent users, had a paltry monthly revenue of only 3 million RMB. Next year, when it reaches its peak, its monthly revenue would still barely reach 10 million RMB.

Comparing *Audition Online* and *PopKart*, it seems you really need women to stimulate consumption.

If you compared the payment rate of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* to that of *PopKart*, it was actually much higher. With the same number of concurrent users, the revenue of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* was more than three times that of *PopKart*!

After receiving the news from Youke, an editor at 17173 even wrote an article.

It listed the peak concurrent user rankings of online games in mainland China since their inception—

*Fantasy Westward Journey* 1.31 million. *Crazy Arcade* 800,000. *QQ Fantasy* 680,000. *The Legend of Mir 2* 670,000. *Westward Journey Online II* 650,000. *World of Warcraft* 600,000. *Yulgang* 520,000. *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* 500,000. *MapleStory* 500,000…

In this list, some games were already on their last legs. For example, *Yulgang*.

Some games surged and then plummeted. For example, *QQ Fantasy*.

*Legends of the Three Kingdoms* actually managed to tie for eighth place with *MapleStory*.

However, *Audition Online* and *PopKart* had not yet reached their full potential. At their peak, both games could achieve a million concurrent users.

*Reign of Hegemon*, *ZT Online*, and *Eudemons Online* were also still growing continuously.

Regardless, with Youke releasing these figures, the industry could no longer look down on them.

In terms of real-time data at that moment, the PCU (Peak Concurrent Users) of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* had already shot up to third place.

Second only to *Fantasy Westward Journey* and *World of Warcraft*!

An editor from *Play* magazine wrote an article full of praise: "I'm a veteran gamer, but I rarely play online games. I played on the Famicom and in arcades as a child, and then moved on to single-player PC games as I grew up. *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* is the online game I've played the longest, though to be precise, it's a tabletop game…"

"For a tabletop game to exceed 500,000 peak concurrent users is truly surprising. The data behind it is terrifying; monthly active users are estimated to be around two to three million. This is extrapolated from Chen Guiliang's interview, where he said that the ratio of monthly active users for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* is very high, far exceeding that of typical online games…"

"Admittedly, this time it benefited from the tailwind of *Xinwen Lianbo*, and other newspapers followed suit in the debate. But if *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* can retain these new players, this will become a landmark event in the Chinese gaming industry…"

"In an era dominated by MMOs, casual online games like *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* are extremely precious and deserve to be cherished by all casual players… Moreover, Chen Guiliang revealed at ChinaJoy that Youke is about to make a single-player game. That's what I'm most looking forward to."

"Currently, Game Science has fewer than 200 employees. I hear they're expanding again recently, but they're still a medium-sized game developer. Give it time, and I believe Youke can grow into a major game company…"

The information Chen Guiliang had was much more detailed than what the reporters and editors knew.

Two weeks later, once the media hype had completely died down, Chen Guiliang listened to a detailed report:

"As the media frenzy fermented, combined with our promotional activities, the PCU of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* continued to rise to a peak of 530,000. The next day, it fell back to just under 500,000, dropped to 460,000 on the third day, and 410,000 on the fourth day… It's clear that many new players came purely out of curiosity after seeing the news."

"But on Friday night, it rose back to 450,000. Saturday was 470,000, Sunday 460,000. The numbers are very stable. It's currently summer vacation, and the fact that it can rebound and maintain these numbers on weekends indicates that most of the new users are working adults."

"Second week. On Monday, it dropped precipitously to 310,000, then hovered around 330,000. Over the three days of the weekend, the evening numbers were around 420,000. This is the data after the hype has passed and everything has completely stabilized…"

"This promotion, originating from *Xinwen Lianbo*, has resulted in a stable increase of 150,000 in PCU for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*. An increase of 83%."

"We've made a killing this time!"

After hearing these figures, Chen Guiliang couldn't help but mutter, "CCTV is awesome!"

What was mentioned here were the daily peak concurrent users; the actual number of new players was far greater.

Moreover, the ratios between registered users, monthly active users, daily active users, and peak concurrent users for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* were unique among all online games.

If you were to analyze it using conventional industry experience, it would leave the executives of major game companies baffled.

Regardless, they had indeed made a killing this time.

With a large number of new users buying card packs and items, this month's revenue for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* was likely to approach 20 million RMB. The champion skin was still in production and would only officially go on sale next month. Therefore, next month's revenue might remain at or exceed 20 million RMB.

There was still a long way to go to catch up with *Audition Online*, but a solid step had been taken.

"Announce it," Chen Guiliang said.

That day, *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* released an official announcement:

From now on, one new hero will be released each month, instead of saving them up for a new card pack (10 heroes per pack). For the first three months after a new hero is released, they cannot be synthesized using Hero Soul Fragments and must be purchased directly with money.

However, each new hero will have a 7-day free trial period, so even free-to-play players can enjoy them for a week.

Once 10 new heroes have been released, they will be made into a physical card pack for sale.

Additionally, special heroes will be released from time to time. For example, during this year's National Day holiday, "SP Sun Shangxiang" will be released.

The editor who wrote the game announcement also helpfully noted: SP Sun Shangxiang is the Shu Kingdom version of the hero after her marriage.

After reading the announcement, most players expressed their support.

Waiting a full six months for 10 new heroes to suddenly be released, versus getting one new hero each month, which meant only 6 in half a year. People preferred the latter because there was something new every month!

Who the hell would wait half a year for you?

What's more, there would be occasional special heroes.

As for new heroes being purchase-only for the first three months, the free-to-play players said they didn't mind. They didn't have enough Hero Soul Fragments anyway, and some heroes required so many fragments that they could bankrupt a free-to-play player!

Besides, they could try them for free for seven days, which made the free-to-play players very happy.

"SP Sun Shangxiang is actually a Shu-faction hero. Doesn't Xiangxiang care about her father and brother anymore?"

"A daughter married is like water thrown out. A Shu-faction Sun Shangxiang is very realistic."

"Who wants to guess SP Sun Shangxiang's skills?"

"It's hard to guess, who knows how Chen Shiyi designed her. By the way, could the special heroes be designed by someone else? Chen Shiyi can't possibly have designed all the cards for Legends of the Three Kingdoms by himself, right?"

"It seems that Youke's Legends of the Three Kingdoms team currently has no hero designers. The so-called designers now are all responsible for designing card art and skins."

"Haha, CEO Chen has been collecting design submissions from players. But he also said he won't be using player suggestions for now, not until he's exhausted his own stash of ideas."

"This is one thing I really admire about Chen Shiyi. Damn, he's running two companies, still has to study, and has to find time to write *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*. And he still has time to design so many hero cards."

"He's pretty incredible."

"Aren't the fourth and fifth volumes of *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty* coming out soon?"

"The 20th of this month. Dangdang is already taking pre-orders."

"Dude, you guys gotta check out the new skins after the game update. The characters are shiny!"

"Really? I'm going to check it out."

Releasing animated skins in 2006 was impossible.

With the current technology, the cost to create one animated skin would be fifty to sixty thousand RMB.

And even if they were made, the computers and internet speeds of some players wouldn't be able to handle them. If someone in a game room had an animated skin, players with junk computers and slow internet would just lag to death.
